userStories.title: Implement search_knowledge_base tool with LlamaIndex hybrid retrieval
userStories.description: As an agent, I need hybrid (BM25 + vector) retrieval over a local knowledge folder.
acceptanceCriteria: Create backend/tools/search_knowledge_base.py exporting a tool named `search_knowledge_base`
Index files from backend/knowledge/ (PDF, MD, TXT) using LlamaIndex Core
Implement Hybrid Search combining BM25Retriever and a VectorIndexRetriever

Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented backend/tools/search_knowledge_base.py as a `@tool("search_knowledge_base")` that builds a QueryFusionRetriever combining BM25Retriever (llama-index-retrievers-bm25 0.7.x) and VectorIndexRetriever over `backend/knowledge/`. The VectorStoreIndex is persisted under `backend/storage/` and reloaded from `docstore.json` on subsequent calls. `_configure_settings()` sets `Settings.llm = MockLLM()` and falls back to `MockEmbedding(embed_dim=384)` when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset so the tool never crashes from missing credentials — BM25 still does real keyword retrieval. QueryFusionRetriever uses `num_queries=1` to bypass LLM-based query rewriting and `mode='reciprocal_rerank'`. Empty/missing knowledge folder returns the fixed `EMPTY_KB_MESSAGE` string. Re-exported from `backend/tools/__init__.py` (`__all__` resorted: fetch_url, python_repl, read_file, search_knowledge_base, terminal). Added `backend/knowledge/.gitkeep` so the layout matches the PRD; `backend/storage/` was already gitignored. 4 unittest cases in backend/tests/test_search_knowledge_base.py: empty-dir, missing-dir, keyword retrieval of a seeded markdown file, and persisted-storage check. All 18 backend tests pass.

userStories.title: Implement Skills bootstrap that generates SKILLS_SNAPSHOT.md
userStories.description: As the system, I need to scan backend/skills/ at startup and produce the available_skills XML snapshot.
acceptanceCriteria: Create backend/skills_loader.py with a function `build_skills_snapshot() -> str`
Scan backend/skills/*/SKILL.md, parse YAML frontmatter for `name` and `description`
Emit <available_skills> XML with one <skill> block per discovered SKILL.md
Each <location> uses a relative path like `./backend/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
Write result to backend/workspace/SKILLS_SNAPSHOT.md
Add a unit test with a fixture skill folder asserting correct XML output
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes:
Implemented backend/skills_loader.py with `build_skills_snapshot(skills_dir=None, *, write=True, snapshot_path=None) -> str`. Scans `skills_dir/*/SKILL.md` (sorted), parses YAML frontmatter via `yaml.safe_load` (PyYAML is a stable transitive of langchain-core / langchain-community / langchain-classic / llama-index-core — not pinned directly to avoid expanding US-002's dep set). `_FRONTMATTER_RE = r'\A---[ 	]*
(.*?)
---[ 	]*(?:
|\Z)'` handles both trailing-newline and EOF-terminated frontmatter blocks. `name` defaults to the skill folder name when frontmatter is missing/invalid; `description` defaults to empty string. `location` is always emitted as `./backend/skills/<folder>/SKILL.md` so the agent's `read_file` tool (root_dir=PROJECT_ROOT) can resolve it directly — even when tests pass a temp `skills_dir`. XML special chars are escaped via `xml.sax.saxutils.escape`. Missing/non-directory skills_dir returns the empty `<available_skills>
</available_skills>` wrapper instead of crashing (matches US-008 graceful-empty pattern). 7 unittest cases in backend/tests/test_skills_loader.py: valid frontmatter, alphabetical sort across multiple skills, empty dir, missing dir, missing frontmatter falls back to folder name, XML-escaping of `<` `&` `"`, and write-to-disk persistence. All 25 backend tests pass. Seeded `backend/workspace/SKILLS_SNAPSHOT.md` with the (currently empty) wrapper by running the bootstrap once.

userStories.notes: Implemented backend/prompt_assembler.py with `build_system_prompt() -> str`. Reads the six source files in the PRD §4.2 order (SKILLS_SNAPSHOT → SOUL → IDENTITY → USER → AGENTS → MEMORY) from `WORKSPACE_DIR` / `MEMORY_DIR` module-level constants, separates each with a `# === <name> ===` header, and truncates any single file longer than `MAX_FILE_CHARS = 20_000` by slicing to the limit and appending the literal `...[truncated]` marker. userStories.title: Implement session JSON persistence
userStories.description: As the system, I need to load and save conversation history per session as JSON arrays.
acceptanceCriteria: Create backend/sessions_store.py with `load_session(name) -> list` and `append_message(name, message)`
Sessions are stored at backend/sessions/{session_name}.json as a JSON array

userStories.notes: Implemented backend/sessions_store.py exposing `load_session(name) -> list[dict[str, Any]]` and `append_message(name, message) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`. Sessions stored at backend/sessions/{name}.json as JSON arrays. Loading non-existent sessions returns [] (no exception). append_message lazily creates SESSIONS_DIR + the JSON file on first call and writes atomically via .tmp + Path.replace so a crash mid-write can't corrupt an existing session. SESSIONS_DIR is a module-level constant (not a default arg) so tests can patch.object it (per Codebase Patterns US-008/US-011). Session names restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (rejects `..`, `/`, empty, etc.) — prevents path traversal out of SESSIONS_DIR; ALLOWED_ROLES = ('user', 'assistant', 'tool'). Tests in backend/tests/test_sessions_store.py — 11 unittest cases across LoadSessionTests (missing/existing/corrupt-JSON/empty-file), AppendMessageTests (first-call file creation, multi-role extend, Unicode + ordering roundtrip with ensure_ascii=False, role rejection, non-dict rejection), SessionNameValidationTests (traversal rejection + typical-name acceptance). All 44 backend tests pass.
